note: vLLM could not be run on this machine or measured first-party. Attempted `pip install vllm` and it failed to even build here (pins torch==2.6.0, unavailable for this Python/platform) -- and vLLM has no Apple Silicon/MPS support regardless, it targets CUDA/ROCm. No CUDA GPU was accessible in this environment (no Colab/cloud GPU access available to this tool). The vLLM-side numbers below are therefore NOT measured by this project -- they are cited from a public third-party benchmark, explicitly labeled as external, and are NOT apples-to-apples with the metal-inference-server numbers (different model size, different hardware tier). This is stated plainly rather than implying a comparison that isn't one.

metal_inference_server.source: measured on this machine, this repo, v0.2 continuous batching
metal_inference_server.hardware: Apple Silicon (M-series), unified memory, MPS backend

vllm_external_citation.source_type: third-party public benchmark, not run by this project

honest_comparison.raw_ratio: vLLM/A5000 measured ~59x higher total throughput than metal-inference-server/Apple-Silicon at c=50
confounds_not_controlled_for: model size: 3B params (vLLM citation) vs 0.5B params (this project) -- a 6x larger model
hardware tier: dedicated 24GB datacenter/workstation GPU (A5000, ~27 TFLOPS FP16) vs a laptop's shared unified-memory integrated GPU

kernel maturity: vLLM's PagedAttention uses fused custom CUDA kernels; this project's paged KV cache (v0.3) explicitly does NOT have a fused kernel and gathers/writes in Python (documented as a throughput cost in v0.3's own results)
output length: vLLM benchmark used 600-token outputs vs 32-token outputs in this project's throughput runs
honest_comparison.conclusion: This is not an apples-to-apples number and isn't presented as one. The realistic takeaway: a hand-rolled Python serving stack on a laptop's integrated GPU, running a 6x smaller model, is not competitive with a production CUDA kernel stack (vLLM) on a dedicated datacenter GPU -- that gap is expected and reported plainly rather than spun to look closer than it is. The value of this project is demonstrating the serving-systems techniques (continuous batching, paged KV, quantization, cancellation, routing, observability) correctly and measuring their real tradeoffs on hardware none of the mainstream engines support natively, not claiming throughput parity with a mature CUDA-native engine.
